title: So bad it’s good: How the Chinese cow movie ‘Niu Lai’ became a box office hit
description:
Niu Lai, a low-budget Chinese animation film about a cow in a dream sequence, is going viral. Released on August 5, it earned less than $1,500 in its first ten days. But then — following snarky comments, bad reviews and widespread mockery by Gen-Z — the film found a larger audience and has now brought in more than $1.6 million dollars.

We speak with William Lee Adams, a BBC culture reporter, and Mengchen Zhang from the BBC’s Global China Unit. They discuss the film’s plot, its rudimentary animation and how bad publicity has helped it go viral at home and abroad. We also hear about the origins of the film, which was made by a mother and son over the course of five years.

Plus: Chinese content creator Marcelo Wang offers his hot take, and Utah-based content creator Cameron Cowley shares three of his favourite “so bad they’re good” films.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討中國低預算動畫電影 Niu Lai 如何因「爛到極致反而好看」而在網路暴紅並創造票房奇蹟。該片由一對缺乏專業背景的母子歷時 5 年製作，講述一隻小牛在夢境中經歷考驗與成長的故事。影片上映前 10 天票房不到 1,500 美元，但隨後經由 Z 世代網民的嘲諷、負面評價與迷因傳播，引發大量關注，累積票房超過 160 萬美元。節目中，主持人 Iqra Farooq 與 BBC 文化記者 William Lee Adams 及全球中國單位的 Mengchen Zhang 討論了該片粗糙的動畫視覺效果、製作背景，以及在 AI 內容充斥與當前年輕人「躺平」現象及經濟壓力下，這部具備真摯情感與懷舊感作品所引發的共鳴。此外，中國內容創作者 Marcello Wang 分享了對該片的看法，美國影評創作者 Cameron Cowley 也分享了他心中 3 部「爛到變經典」的電影清單。
summaryEn: This episode of the BBC podcast What in the World explores how Niu Lai, a low-budget Chinese animated film created over five years by an amateur mother-and-son duo, unexpectedly became a box-office hit. After grossing less than $1,500 in its first ten days, the movie went viral through online mockery, bad reviews, and memes among Chinese Gen-Z audiences, eventually earning over $1.6 million. Host Iqra Farooq, BBC culture reporter William Lee Adams, and Mengchen Zhang from the BBC Global China Unit break down the film's rudimentary animation and plot, discussing how its raw, human charm offers comfort in an era of polished AI content and economic uncertainties. Additionally, Chinese creator Marcello Wang provides his perspective on the film, and US content creator Cameron Cowley shares three of his favorite 'so bad they're good' movies.
